elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 5.1(a): IBM "will perform the Services using reasonable care and skill ... the degree of knowledge, skill and judgment customarily exercised by members of the applicable profession with respect to work of a similar nature" — substantively the professional/workmanlike standard.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "any software provided to Customer as part of the Services (including the software portions of the Base Components) will conform in all material respects to its documentation".

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Inserted period is "ninety (90) days following delivery", not twelve months.
Inserted Services duration is "at least thirty (30) days following performance of the applicable Services", short of 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "IBM will, at its option, repair or replace the non-conforming software or re-perform the non-conforming Services".
Inserted: "or refund the charges paid for the non-conforming software or Services".

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: The rationale asserts Section 5.1 contains compliance-with-laws covenants, but the cited/rendered text of 5.1 shows only the care-and-skill warranty (a) and the corporate authority representation (b); no compliance-with-laws language is visible in the operative text supplied.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code / virus warranty appears anywhere in the rendered Section 5.1 or the inserted text.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Insertion: "for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, any software provided to Customer as part of the Services ... will conform in all material respects to its documentation".

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Insertion: "the warranty in Subsection 5.1(a) will apply for at least thirty (30) days following performance of the applicable Services" — an express duration anchored to performance, attached to the retained care-and-skill warranty.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "IBM will, at its option, repair or replace the non-conforming software or re-perform the non-conforming Services".
"or refund the charges paid for the non-conforming software or Services".

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete in operative language: 90-day software-to-documentation warranty, ≥30-day Services warranty tied to the retained 5.1(a) standard, and repair/replace (or re-performance) plus refund remedies, all inside Section 5.1 so the 5.2 exclusivity sentence does not strip them.

Preferred level is not reached: software duration is 90 days rather than 12 months, Services duration is 30 days rather than 90 days, no malicious-code warranty was added, and a compliance-with-laws warranty is not visible in the supplied 5.1 text. These are level gaps only, not defects in the chosen fallback target.

Minimality holds. The insertion is a single concise sentence pair supplying the missing warranty and remedy, and the four-word carve-out "Except as provided in Section 5.1" in 5.4(c) is required by the checklist logic because the untouched AS IS sentence covers "ALL MATERIALS AND ... SOFTWARE" and would otherwise contradict the new express warranty. No survival tail, expense allocation, procedure or extra damages category was added; existing favourable language (competent personnel, non-IBM supplier warranties) is retained verbatim.

Intent is preserved: the disclaimer, the exclusivity sentence and the non-IBM supplier sentence all survive without contradiction, and the new text cross-references an existing subsection (5.1(a)) rather than creating a dangling reference.

Drafting points to tighten (non-fatal): the inserted paragraph starts lowercase with no subsection letter — label it "c." so the reference in 5.4(c) to "Section 5.1" and the internal reference to "Subsection 5.1(a)" read cleanly; and confirm "Base Components" is a defined term in the Agreement, otherwise delete the parenthetical, which is scope clarification rather than a checklist requirement.

If pressed to the preferred position, the two operative edits needed are: change "ninety (90) days" for software to "twelve (12) months" and "thirty (30) days" for Services to "ninety (90) days", plus add express compliance-with-laws and no-malicious-code warranties.
